title: Leaving Moten and going to New York to Willie Bryant
summary: He left four weeks before Moten died, wanting something bigger, and went to New York at Bryant's request, where union transfer rules limited his playing.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, when you -- now, do you stay with Morton up until the time he dies?
I left four weeks before he died.

Well, I was kind of a rolling stone, you know? Like, after you play with a band so long, I say, man, this band is at a standstill, I want to find something bigger and more exciting. I'd heard Duke Ellington, you know, and I wanted to leave because I said, the band has got all you need. Say, all right, give me some good arrangements if you got to leave me. I say, well, I'll leave you Pat. And that's when Buster was there, we all got together with things like Morton Swing and a few of those things, and Lafayette, some of those kind of things, Blue Room. Hershel used to sing all those things, too. Am I Blue and all of them.
And then I went to New York. I think Willie Pratt sent for me, and that's when he had the band -- and Billy Carter was in his band. Teddy Wilson and Cozy Coles and Battles.

And Willy sent for me and I came to New York. But I had a little trouble with the union, with the transfer. So I just wrote that (unintelligible) in the Chapel and stuff like that, and he recorded. I was down there, so I got paid on the payroll anyway. And a lot of nights, I'd play a little trombone, but the union was always on top of me. So I played piano. Sometimes I'd play piano with the band. And I used to play (unintelligible) with Teddy Wilson --
